limitations: New V2 disposable cross-process run after accepted pipe-rights repair; old V1 ERROR and its retained work stay immutable.
Both exact original reports (6d1376 PASS and 7ec ERROR) are required before compilation, native execution and cleanup.
Four raw pipe endpoints must close in a fixed prefix before the unchanged 12-role close sequence. No arbitrary extra closes.
Fourteen repaired native C# sources unchanged from 6d1376. Only coordinator and receiver compile; no managed or historical suite runs.
One fresh directory/empty gate file. Parent closes fixture streams before launching the coordinator.
One dedicated coordinator creates one receiver using exact three-handle list and job-at-creation; no broad-inheritance fallback.
Outer PID/creation checked through Popen-owned handle; receiver identity/exit checked by accepted coordinator and matched raw GH1 replies.
The outer launcher does not independently query the receiver process handle. On error it does not infer receiver exit from coordinator exit.
Receiver close and exit are separate events; post-exit exclusive probe is gated by confirmed clean receiver completion.
Read/write access is requested for the sharing probe, but no gate data is written; only IPC endpoints receive protocol writes.
Normal success does not exercise kill-on-job-close, forced pending, crashes, durability or installation protection.
Unknown completion, timeout, nonzero exit, kill, extra output, drift or cleanup error never passes; remaining files are retained.
CPython 3.12.10 lstat identities and source hashes are point-in-time bindings, not runtime/loader attestation or hostile same-user protection.
No parent-side descriptor or alternate-data-stream enumeration. Ordinary entries/content/metadata are checked before/after.
Compiler/CLR/kernel may use OS services. Fixed protocol deadlines do not guarantee interruption of kernel/process creation stalls.
Repeat guard is not a concurrency lock; preserve partial or ERROR evidence and do not automatically repeat.
